Table 1: Comparison with state-of-the-art VSR methods on LRS3. † indicates the use of additional video-level metadata, such as title, description, and speaker name. ‡ indicates our reproduction trained using only LRS3.
Table 8: Validation WER (%) of length-guided reranking weights on LRS3 with AV-HuBERT. The best validation setting is (λ, β) = (0.9, 0.7), yielding 11.73% validation WER and 21.89% test WER.
Table 9: Validation WER (%) of length-guided reranking weights on LRS3 with USR 2.0. The best validation setting is (λ, β) = (0.9, 0.6), yielding 16.04% validation WER and 19.50% test WER.
Table 10: Validation WER (%) of length-guided reranking weights on LRS2 with USR 2.0. The best validation setting is (λ, β) = (1.0, 0.9), yielding 22.83% validation WER and 16.83% test WER.

Figure 2: Overview of DLLM-VSR. (a) Overall architecture with a frozen visual encoder, a length adapter, FC projection layers, and a LoRA-adapted DLLM decoder. (b) Confidence-based unmasking, where high-confidence positions are committed first and the committed tokens are used as bidirectional textual context. (c) Two-stage masked-denoising training for visual-to-text content alignment and length-aware sequence completion. (d) Lengthguided candidate decoding with multiple length hypotheses and joint candidate reranking.
